role: Small owner-operator, private investor and 1031 agent
deployer: A two-principal Phoenix investment shop (fictional) that owns about 140 apartment units across five small multifamily properties and runs a Python agent over its own deal pipeline.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
top_tasks: Track 45-day identification and 180-day exchange deadlines and test identification rules for a sale-to-buy 1031
Compute boot, debt replacement and boot-limited gain for a proposed replacement purchase
Size acquisition financing on a 20-40 unit replacement property under LTV, DSCR and debt-yield tests
hardest_task: The firm sold a 24-unit Phoenix property for $4.2M (selling costs $252,000, debt payoff $2.1M, adjusted basis about $1.9M) on 2026-09-15 and must close a replacement by the 180-day mark. The agent has to keep three candidate properties (about $4.5M, $2.6M and a third) inside the 3-property or 200% test, show boot and debt replacement for a $4.5M purchase with $2.3M new debt, and size that loan at a roughly $297,000 NOI, with every figure the partners can hand to their QI and CPA.
data_it_needs: Deadline arithmetic that handles the tax-return-due-date cap, identification tests that exclude late identifications, boot and debt-replacement netting, loan sizing; later Maricopa County owner and sales records for replacement candidates.
dealbreakers: A confident wrong deadline; unexplained numbers with no steps; anything that tells the partners an exchange qualifies.
budget_note: Small shop; would pay a few tens of dollars a month only if it saves a CPA or QI hour; free tier acceptable for a handful of calls per deal.

deployer: The asset management group of a fictional institutional apartment owner (about 9,000 units nationally) that runs an in-house Python agent to prepare monthly asset-manager packages.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
top_tasks: Turn the monthly rent roll into GPR, loss to lease, concessions, occupancy and an expiration ladder
Check a JV equity waterfall for LP and GP splits before the quarterly investor report
Quote the effective rent after concessions on a proposed lease renewal or new lease
hardest_task: For a 180-unit Los Angeles apartment property the agent must produce the month-end package: GPR about $520,000 a month, 11 to 14 expiring leases a month, 5 to 9 units on notice, loss to lease and amortised concessions by floor plan, and a view of how a 36-month JV waterfall ($12M of equity, 90/10 LP/GP, 8% pref, 80/20 to a 15% LP IRR, 70/30 after) pays out on three sale scenarios. Every number must tie to Yardi within a dollar.
data_it_needs: Rent roll analytics that reconcile to Yardi, concession treatment on both amortised and cash bases, waterfall splits, LA County parcel and ownership context for comps.
dealbreakers: Numbers that do not tie to Yardi, undisclosed conventions, input limits below a property's unit count, silent normalisation of bad input.
budget_note: Institutional budget; Pro at $49 a month is noise if it replaces an analyst hour a week, but needs vendor and security review first.

deployer: A fictional mid-market Midwest brokerage team that sells student housing near Mizzou, KU, Wash U and SLU campuses and runs a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent that drafts BOV pricing pages for its brokers.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Draft a BOV pricing page: value at three cap rates, price per bed and implied cap rate on the ask
Estimate what loan a buyer can get on a 300-bed asset and the sensitivity to rate and NOI
Produce a buyer's 5-year unlevered return for the offering memorandum
hardest_task: A broker lists a 312-bed, 96-unit Columbia, MO asset at $31.2M ($100,000 per bed) with stabilized NOI of $1,872,000 before a $93,600 reserve ($300 per bed). The agent has to show value at 6.0%, 6.25% and 6.5% caps, the implied cap on ask, deductions for $250,000 of lease-up and $180,000 of deferred roof work, the debt a buyer can raise at 6.25% (65% LTV, 1.30x DSCR), and an unlevered five-year IRR for the OM, all by Friday.
data_it_needs: Direct cap and debt sizing math, per-bed pricing, closed student-housing sales comps in Columbia, Lawrence and St. Louis, lender quotes.
dealbreakers: A tool that cannot be reached from Copilot Studio, per-seat pricing, no student-housing comps, results a client could challenge.
budget_note: Brokerage pays for data (CoStar, RCA); calculators alone are worth little unless they are free and fast to wire.

deployer: A fictional mid-market tenant-rep brokerage in Charlotte whose brokers use Claude Desktop with a shared custom connector to prepare proposal comparisons and renew-versus-relocate analyses for suburban office clients.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Rank three or four landlord proposals for a 15,000 to 25,000 sf office tenant on one effective-cost basis, gross vs NNN vs base year
Renew versus relocate analysis for a tenant with a 2027 expiry
Check a CAM reconciliation or a base-year opex pass-through the landlord sent
hardest_task: A professional-services client needs 18,000 RSF in Ballantyne for a 7-year term starting 2027-07-01. Three proposals arrive on different structures (full-service at $31.00, NNN at $22.50 plus $11.50 opex, base-year at $26.00), with different free rent (6, 4, 5 months), TI ($55, $60 and $50 per RSF) and load factors (1.14, 1.12, 1.15). The broker must rank them on usable-sf effective cost and compare the winner with the client's renewal at $27.50.
data_it_needs: Proposal comparison with mixed opex structures, renew vs relocate, CAM audit math; Charlotte and Raleigh asking-rent and concession comps.
dealbreakers: Results the broker cannot explain to the client in one page, undisclosed treatment of TI and opex, any per-seat cost.
budget_note: Brokers pay for CoStar; a calculator is worth a few tens of dollars a month only if it replaces the Excel template.

deployer: A fictional mid-market Atlanta developer of build-to-rent communities (single-family rental homes on 15 to 40 acre sites) that uses a Claude Desktop connector for first-pass feasibility on land deals.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Compute yield on cost and development spread for a 140-home BTR scheme
Size and schedule a construction-to-mini-perm loan
Run a stabilised 5-year unlevered DCF and test value against cost
hardest_task: A 140-home BTR community on a 28-acre site in north metro Atlanta: all-in cost $42.0M ($300,000 a home, 196,000 sf), stabilised NOI of about $2.64M, a 5.25% market cap rate and a $27.3M mini-perm (65% of cost, 6.75%, 24 months interest-only, 60-month term). The agent must show yield on cost, value created, the debt schedule and a five-year DCF, and flag what zoning and entitlement data are missing.
data_it_needs: Yield and spread math, loan schedule, DCF, plus parcel, zoning, utility and comparable BTR lease data for Georgia counties.
dealbreakers: Results the agent cannot tie to the spreadsheet; no parcel or zoning lookup for site screening; math that assumes an office rent roll.
budget_note: Land-acquisition team pays for parcel data. Calculators alone are not worth budget.

deployer: A five-person fictional New York investment firm buying 20 to 60 unit rent-stabilised and free-market apartment buildings in the outer boroughs, with analysts who run Claude Code in a repo of underwriting scripts.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
top_tasks: Size debt on a 42-unit Bronx walk-up from NOI, LTV, DSCR and debt yield, and stress it
Value the building at a cap rate and read the implied cap on the ask, before and after reserves
Check LL97 and rent-stabilisation exposure before bid
hardest_task: A 42-unit Bronx building is offered at $9.8M on trailing NOI of $510,000 (5.2% before a $10,500 reserve, 38,000 sf). The lender quotes 6.25% on 30-year amortization at 70% LTV, 1.20x DSCR and 8% debt yield. The agent must size the loan, show how it shrinks under -5% and -10% NOI and +75 bp, value the building at a 5.5% cap, and flag NYC Local Law 97 exposure; every number needs a formula ID and steps the principal can audit.
data_it_needs: Debt sizing with stress, direct cap with reserves, LL97 limits and penalty arithmetic, ACRIS deeds and mortgages for comps, DHCR registration data for stabilised units.
dealbreakers: A skill or doc that quotes figures the live service does not return; confident output with no steps; silent assumptions; slow or unreliable calls in the middle of a bid.
budget_note: Small shop; pays for data (PropertyShark, CoStar). A calculator is free money only if it is right; would pay a little for ACRIS-backed lookups.

deployer: A fictional national industrial brokerage group that runs a LangGraph workflow with MCP adapters to assemble portfolio offering packages across Memphis, Columbus, the Lehigh Valley and the Inland Empire.
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
top_tasks: Compute WALT and rollover exposure for a multi-building portfolio
Convert lease terms to net effective rent for comps used in the offering memorandum
Package comps so the team can share them across offices with rights stated
hardest_task: Five single-tenant industrial buildings (1.47M sf, $10.39M of annual rent) in four markets are going to market as a portfolio. The agent must compute rent-weighted and area-weighted WALT, show that two leases (150,000 sf and 96,000 sf) roll within 14 months, normalise a recent 250,000 sf Inland Empire lease to net effective rent for the OM, and pull sales and lease comps by address for each building.
data_it_needs: WALT and NER math, a comp format the team can validate and share, and the address-keyed comps and ownership that come with a registry.
dealbreakers: A tool list too big to load into a framework's context; no way to look up comps by address; errors the framework cannot parse.
budget_note: The group already pays CoStar and Reonomy; calculators and comp formats are free-tier material, comps by address would be the paid piece.

role: Due diligence and legal review agent
deployer: The real estate practice group of a fictional mid-size Texas law firm that runs an OpenAI Agents SDK workflow to abstract leases and check tenant estoppels for buyers of grocery-anchored centers.
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
incumbent_tools: Kira-style lease abstraction (as a product category)
top_tasks: Abstract an anchor lease and its amendments to the current state with a quote and page for every term
Compare a tenant estoppel with the lease and list the mismatches
Check a proposed in-line tenant against the anchor's exclusive and prohibited uses
hardest_task: A buyer is acquiring a 212,000 sf grocery-anchored center in San Antonio. The anchor lease is 140 pages with three amendments (term extension, rent reset and a second exclusive); the estoppel states a different expiration date. The agent must produce the current-state abstract with controlling citations, flag every estoppel mismatch, and screen 9 pending in-line tenants against the exclusives in 48 hours.
data_it_needs: Quote-and-page checking of agent-extracted terms, amendment precedence, estoppel comparison, exclusive-use screening; ideally the PDF reading.
dealbreakers: A tool that reports a term as verified when it checked nothing; no way to trace a value to a page; confidential lease text stored or logged.
budget_note: Billable-hour firm: pays if it demonstrably cuts review time and passes a client security review; the hosted tool processes text in memory per its privacy page.

deployer: An acquisitions group inside a fictional mid-market owner of about 60 manufactured housing communities, with analysts who run Claude Code against broker packages from several states.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
temperament: skeptical: has been burned by confident-but-wrong tools; assumes a claim is false until a call proves it
incumbent_tools: Yardi/Rent Manager exports for lot rent rolls
top_tasks: Turn a broker's lot rent roll into GPR, occupancy, loss to lease and a month-to-month versus lease split
Value a community by direct cap with reserves and read the implied cap on the ask
Run a five-year unlevered DCF and test the broker's pro forma
hardest_task: A 180-lot all-age community in a second-tier market is offered at $14.9M on a T-12 NOI of $1.02M. Lot rent averages $710 on 150 occupied lots against $775 market, with roughly 40% of residents month-to-month and the rest on 12-month leases, 6 lots offline after a flood, and park-owned homes mixed in. The agent must tie the broker's rent roll to the T-12, strip what does not belong in the NOI, and show value at 6.0% to 6.75% caps with a $250-a-lot reserve.
data_it_needs: Lot rent roll analytics that handle month-to-month tenants, direct cap with reserves, DCF, debt sizing; park, owner and sales records for state-level comps.
dealbreakers: Skills that quote results the live service does not give; output that implies certainty; a rent roll tool that assumes apartments (square feet, 12-month leases).
budget_note: Pays for broker relationships and data; would pay modestly for anything that cuts underwriting hours and is auditable.

deployer: The acquisitions team of a fictional mid-market Dallas office investor that runs a CrewAI crew (rent-roll reader, underwriter, reviewer) against broker offering packages and wants the DCF engine to be a tool, not a spreadsheet.
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
top_tasks: Run a multi-tenant office DCF with rollover, free rent, TI and commissions from a broker rent roll
Size acquisition debt and check the going-in yield against the cost of capital
Stress the exit assumptions and see where the deal clears the hurdle
hardest_task: A 220,000 sf Las Colinas-style suburban office building (fictional) is offered at $52.0M ($236 per sf). The rent roll has five lines: a 42,000 sf law firm at $27.50 NNN (38 months left), a 31,000 sf engineer at $26.00 NNN (20 months), a 28,000 sf medical group at $29.00 on a base year of $9.00 (71 months), 24,000 vacant sf, and a 95,000 sf insurer at $24.50 NNN (15 months, 2 free months left). With 65% renewal probability, 9 months' downtime, 8 months free and $55 new-tenant TI, the agent must produce a 7-year unlevered DCF at an 8.75% discount rate and 7.75% exit cap, and see whether the deal clears a 7.5% unlevered IRR hurdle.
data_it_needs: A DCF whose rollover, free-rent, TI and recovery conventions are stated and reproducible; debt sizing; ideally DFW comps and ownership.
dealbreakers: A DCF that cannot be tied out line by line; hidden conventions; no way to override a lease's rollover assumptions.
budget_note: ARGUS is already paid for; would pay for an auditable engine an agent can call and for DFW registry data.

deployer: The commercial property underwriting desk of a fictional Houston-based specialty insurer that uses a small Python service to pre-screen submissions for mixed-use buildings in Gulf Coast metros.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
temperament: pragmatic: cares only whether it saves time on the job this week
incumbent_tools: a catastrophe model vendor's API (as a product category)
top_tasks: Key each submitted building to a stable ID so flood, wind and prior-loss data join across systems
Check replacement cost and insured value against the submission
Record flood zone and elevation facts with their source and usage rights
hardest_task: A broker submits a 5-story mixed-use building near Buffalo Bayou, ground-floor retail and 60 apartments above, 88,000 sf, TIV $24M. The agent must identify the building across the FEMA flood map, the appraisal district record and the submission, check the stated replacement cost of about $265 per sf, and attach cited facts (flood zone, first-floor elevation, year built) to the file with rights stated.
data_it_needs: Building and parcel identity for Harris County, flood zone and elevation, replacement-cost benchmarks, year built, construction class and prior losses.
dealbreakers: No hazard or replacement-cost data at all; IDs that do not match the county's records.
budget_note: Pays catastrophe-model and data vendors; would pay little for identity and fact plumbing alone.
